taxonomic_note: Current Kew/POWO, ITIS and Flora of North America accept Heteranthera dubia; older segregate Zosterella and H. graminea names are synonyms.
look_here_first: In flower, look for a single yellow star/salver-shaped flower emerging from linear aquatic foliage. Joey's close views add a striking second cue: paired plants can show mirror-image style/anther handedness.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays — peer-reviewed San Marcos River aquatic-plant surveys document Heteranthera dubia, reinforced by Edwards Aquifer Authority monitoring and Joey's Hays County video. Travis — Harvard specimens from Lake Austin/Colorado River at Austin and City of Austin surveys. Comal — Harvard Lindheimer specimens from New Braunfels.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Only exact documented target-zone localities counted.

best_field_traits: yellow salverform perianth with long tube
flowers open early and may wilt by dusk
three equal stamens with anthers that coil after anthesis
few-winged seeds in an elongate capsule
mirror-image flower handedness/enantiostyly visible in Joey comparison
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Linear thin leaves; submerged plants may be more elongate and narrow than emersed forms.
morphology_keys.flower: Yellow, salverform, one-flowered inflorescence; perianth tube can be long and variable with water/temperature.
morphology_keys.fruit: Elongate capsule with relatively few winged seeds.
joey_field_notes: Joey shows whole-plant aquatic habit, then a close flower, then a side-by-side mirror-image flower comparison.
The mirror-image sequence is retained as a structural learning cue rather than as the only identification feature.

comparisons.key_distinctions: H. dubia combines linear sessile leaves with a solitary yellow salverform flower; FNA further separates it by a one-flowered inflorescence, equal stamens and coiling anthers.
